originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact two-series distribution for all unrestricted ordinary palindromes and all fixed alphabet sizes, with its center-parity renewal law. Barker et al. 2020 already prove the palindrome midpoint identity and Adamson 2023 count arches of unrestricted words. Their separate statements do not explicitly state the complete palindrome index counting formulas or limiting parity statistic. Reversal-fixed counting is not implied coefficientwise by the all-words distribution; adjacency-distinct and reverse-complement symmetric enumerations concern different languages. Literature incompleteness and possible unstated corollaries remain risks.

value.rationale: Subsequence universality of palindrome languages is a canonical constrained-language statistic; its joint index and length distribution for the entire unrestricted ordinary-palindrome family (every \(q\ge2\), every length), plus the limiting midpoint-coupon renewal probability, is a complete natural enumeration and asymptotic law. Reversal creates nontrivial center effects not recovered from generic total counts. The value is the exact language invariant, not the individual known midpoint lemma or coupon-collector expectation.
